$780 million</font></div><div style="padding-left:22.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Increased confidence in FY 2026 adjusted</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">2</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> EPS $2.90 &#8211; $3.05  </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8220;Edwards&#8217; strong fourth quarter and full year performance in 2025 reflect our differentiated strategy with a clear vision around three key elements&#58; focusing solely on structural heart, solving large, urgent and very complex patient needs, and pursuing unique opportunities to innovate and lead, all achieved through excellent execution by our deeply experienced teams,&#8221; said Bernard Zovighian, Edwards&#8217; CEO. &#8220;Based on multiple catalysts and the company&#8217;s strong fourth quarter performance, we have increased confidence in our outlook for 2026 and believe that our 70 years of expertise in valve innovation and world-class evidence will create sustainable growth and expanded </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">profitability.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8220;These enduring catalysts benefitting Edwards in 2026 and the years ahead include distinguished long-term results unique to Edwards from the PARTNER 3 7-year and PARTNER 2 10-year trials, the impact of the practice-changing EARLY TAVR trial, new guidelines for treating aortic stenosis patients in Europe and the approvals of the first transcatheter mitral replacement therapy. We expect additional meaningful catalysts later in 2026 to fuel sustainable growth into the future, including next-generation TEER, PASCAL for U.S. tricuspid patients, continued scaling of EVOQUE and the potential of increased patient access from an updated TAVR NCD,&#8221; continued Zovighian.</font></div><div style="height:27pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR)</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">In the fourth quarter, the company reported TAVR sales of $1.16 billion, which grew 12.0% versus the prior year, or 10.6% on a constant currency basis. Full-year 2025 global sales of $4.5 billion increased 8.6% year-over-year on a constant currency basis. U.S. and OUS sales growth rates were similar on a constant currency basis. The company&#8217;s procedural growth was comparable across the U.S. and OUS, and average price and competitive position was stable on a global basis.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">In the U.S., the company saw intentional and urgent treatment of patients with severe aortic stenosis, fueled by a large and growing body of world-class evidence on the SAPIEN platform. The U.S. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) formally opened the process to reconsider the National Coverage Determination for TAVR, a decision that has the potential to improve timely and equitable access to lifesaving TAVR therapy.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:200%">At TCT last October, the 7&#8209;year PARTNER 3 and 10-year PARTNER 2 data confirmed the long&#8209;term durability and proven valve performance of the SAPIEN platform. These data reinforce the confidence that physicians and patients have in Edwards&#8217; TAVR and set a new clinical standard with Edwards&#8217; transcatheter heart valve therapy for safety, efficacy, durability, and lifetime management of patients.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Edwards also expanded its partnership with the American Heart Association as the founding sponsor of the Heart Valve Initiative. This new multi-year initiative is focused on timely diagnosis and treatment to save lives and improve care for millions living with heart valve disease.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">In Europe, fourth quarter results reflected healthy underlying TAVR procedure growth and Edwards&#8217; consistent commercial execution across the region. The company continues to see modest year-over-year share improvement in the wake of a competitor&#8217;s exit. Updated guidelines from the European Society of Cardiology and European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery are reshaping clinical discussions around proactive disease management and reinforcing the role of TAVR for a broader patient population. </font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Therapies (TMTT)</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">The depth and breadth of Edwards&#8217; portfolio of repair and replacement therapies to treat mitral and tricuspid diseases drove another quarter of strong growth. Fourth quarter TMTT sales grew more than 40% to $156 million. Global adoption of PASCAL and EVOQUE contributed to overall growth. The company continues to expand the number of centers and physician training while focusing on excellent patient outcomes.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">The recent FDA approval of SAPIEN M3 expands Edwards&#8217; mitral portfolio in the U.S. and represents the first transcatheter replacement option for patients suffering from mitral disease. Similar to other Edwards therapy launches, the strategic introduction of SAPIEN M3 is leveraging the company&#8217;s proven high value support model and focusing on outstanding clinical outcomes. Edwards is initially </font></div><div style="height:27pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">2</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">opening sites that were previously in the ENCIRCLE pivotal clinical trial, and physician focus and interest in this technology is growing.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">With PASCAL and EVOQUE growing globally, and now with the introduction of SAPIEN M3 in the U.S. and Europe, Edwards continues to deliver on its vision of offering a portfolio of therapies and treating more patients in this globally underserved population with mitral and tricuspid disease. This comprehensive portfolio represents several layers of durable growth. </font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">Surgical</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">In Surgical, fourth quarter global sales from continuing operations of $254 million increased 4% over the prior year, or 2% on a constant currency basis. Full-year Surgical sales of more than $1 billion grew 5%, or 4% on a constant currency basis, driven by continued adoption of RESILIA therapies that offer extended durability of Edwards&#8217; surgical therapies including INSPIRIS, KONECT and MITRIS.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Edwards is pursuing multiple new innovations to advance Surgical solutions for patients, including Left Atrial Appendage Closure (LAAC). This therapeutic area is a complementary solution to specific valvular procedures, and the company is planning on a preliminary introduction of a new surgical LAAC technology later this year.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%;text-decoration:underline">Additional Financial Results</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">For the quarter, the gross profit margin was 78.1%, or 78.3% adjusted, compared to 78.9%, or 79.0% adjusted, in the same period last year. The company continues to expect its full-year 2026 adjusted gross profit margin to be between 78% and 79%.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Selling, general and administrative expenses in the fourth quarter were $603 million, or 38.4% of sales, compared to 35.5% of sales in the prior year. This increase funded strategic investments to amplify patient access to therapy. Some of this strategic spending was delayed from previous quarters in the year. Research and development expenses in the fourth quarter were $268 million, or 17.1% of sales, compared to 19.6% in the prior year. The company continues to expect its full-year 2026 R&#38;D as a percentage of sales to be approximately 17%.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Operating profit margin in the fourth quarter of 9.6%, or 23.7% adjusted, was in line with the company&#8217;s previous guidance of mid-20% for the quarter. Adjusted EPS was $0.58, which also included a higher-than-expected tax rate for the quarter. In 2026, Edwards expects full-year operating profit margin at the high end of the original 28% to 29% guidance range.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Cash and cash equivalents were approximately </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">$3.0&#160;billion</font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> as of Dec. 31, 2025. Total debt was approximately $600 million.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">Outlook</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Edwards has increased confidence in meeting its 2026 sales growth rate guidance of 8 to 10% and EPS guidance of $2.90 to $3.05. For the first quarter of 2026, the company projects total sales to be between $1.55 and $1.63 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.70 to $0.76. </font></div><div style="height:27pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">3</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">About Edwards Lifesciences</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:232%">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Edwards Lifesciences is the leading global structural heart innovation company, driven by a passion to improve patient lives. Through breakthrough technologies, world-class evidence and partnerships with clinicians and healthcare stakeholders, our employees are inspired by our patient-focused culture to deliver life-changing innovations to those who need them most. Discover more at www.edwards.com and follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram and YouTube.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">Conference Call and Webcast Information</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:232%">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">The company will be hosting a conference call today at 2&#58;00&#160;p.m. PT to discuss its fourth quarter results.&#160;To participate in the conference call, dial (877) 704-2848 or (201) 389-0893. style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">6</font></div></div></div><div id="i68e87899cf99498d9560512531881995_10"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:40.5pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">EDWARDS LIFESCIENCES CORPORATION</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Non-GAAP Financial Information</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">To supplement the consolidated financial results prepared in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;), the Company uses non-GAAP historical financial measures. Management makes adjustments to the GAAP measures for items (both charges and gains) that (a) do not reflect the core operational activities of the Company, (b) are commonly adjusted within the Company&#8217;s industry to enhance comparability of the Company&#8217;s financial results with those of its peer group, or (c) are inconsistent in amount or frequency between periods (albeit such items are monitored and controlled with equal diligence relative to core operations). The Company uses the terms &#8220;adjusted&#8221; and &#8220;constant currency&#8221; when referring to non-GAAP sales from continuing operations and sales growth information, respectively, which excludes currency exchange rate fluctuations and newly acquired products. The Company uses the term &#8220;adjusted&#8221; to also exclude certain litigation expenses, amortization of intangible assets, separation costs, intangible assets impairment charges, fair value adjustments to contingent consideration liabilities, loss on impairment, restructuring expenses, charitable contribution to the Edwards Lifesciences Foundation, acquisition contract termination costs, and a gain on remeasurement of previously held interest upon acquisition.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Management uses non-GAAP financial measures internally for strategic decision making, forecasting future results, and evaluating current performance. These non-GAAP financial measures are used in addition to, and in conjunction with, results presented in accordance with GAAP and reflect an additional way of viewing aspects of the Company's operations by investors that, when viewed with its GAAP results, provide a more complete understanding of factors and trends affecting the Company's business and facilitate comparability to historical periods.  </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Non-GAAP financial measures are not prepared in accordance with GAAP&#59; therefore, the information is not necessarily comparable to other companies and should be considered as a supplement to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, the corresponding measures calculated in accordance with GAAP. A reconciliation of non-GAAP historical financial measures to the most comparable GAAP measure is provided in the tables below.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Fluctuations in currency exchange rates impact the comparative results and sales growth rates of the Company's underlying business. Management believes that excluding the impact of currency exchange rate fluctuations from its sales growth provides investors a more useful comparison to historical financial results. The impact of the fluctuations has been detailed in the &#8220;Reconciliation of Sales by Product Group and Region.&#8221;  </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Guidance for sales and sales growth rates is provided on a &#8220;constant currency basis,&#8221; and projections for diluted earnings per share, net income and growth, gross profit margin, and taxes are also provided on a non-GAAP basis, as adjusted, for the items identified above due to the inherent difficulty in forecasting such items without unreasonable efforts. The Company is not able to provide a reconciliation of the non-GAAP guidance to comparable GAAP measures due to the unknown effect, timing, and potential significance of special charges or gains, and management's inability to forecast charges associated with future transactions and initiatives. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">The items described below are adjustments to the GAAP financial results in the reconciliations that follow&#58;</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Certain Litigation Expenses</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company incurred certain litigation expenses of $10.9&#160;million and $8.9&#160;million in the first quarter of 2025 and 2024, respectively, $15.5&#160;million and $8.1&#160;million for the second quarter of 2025 and 2024, respectively, $90.4&#160;million and $10.8&#160;million for the third quarter of 2025 and 2024, respectively, and $208.6&#160;million and $12.6&#160;million in the fourth quarter of 2025 and 2024, respectively. Such expenses relate to intellectual property litigation, settlements, contingencies, and external legal costs.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Amortization of Intangible Assets</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company recorded amortization expense related to developed technology and patents in the amount of $1.4&#160;million and $0.5&#160;million in the first quarter of 2025 and 2024, respectively, $1.8&#160;million and $1.2&#160;million in the second quarter of 2025 and 2024, respectively, $1.7&#160;million and $1.3&#160;million in the third quarter of 2025 and 2024, respectively, and $2.4&#160;million and $1.4&#160;million in the fourth quarter of  2025 and 2024, respectively.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Separation Costs</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">- </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company recorded expenses of $4.2&#160;million in both the first and second quarter of 2025, $0.1&#160;million in the third quarter of 2025, and $19.0&#160;million in the fourth quarter of 2024, related to consulting, legal, tax, and other professional advisory services related to the sale of Critical Care.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Intangible assets impairment charges</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company recorded a $40.0&#160;million charge in the third quarter of 2025 related to an impairment of certain developed technology asset acquired as part of an acquisition. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Change in Fair Value of Contingent Consideration Liabilities</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company recorded a gain of $12.5&#160;million in the third quarter of 2025 related to changes in the fair value of its contingent consideration liabilities arising from acquisitions.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="height:40.5pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">7</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:40.5pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Loss on Impairment</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company recorded loss on impairment of $47.1&#160;million in the second quarter of 2025 ($36.0 million net of tax adjustment), related to the Company's determination to not exercise an option to acquire one of its VIE investments. In addition, the Company recorded $99.8&#160;million ($76.5&#160;million net of tax) in the fourth quarter of 2025, related to impairment of its investment in JenaValve Technologies.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Restructuring Expenses </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">- The Company recorded a $32.9&#160;million charge in the third quarter of 2024 and $8.9&#160;million charge in the fourth quarter of 2025 primarily related to severance expenses associated with a global workforce realignment.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Charitable Foundation Contribution</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company recorded a $30.0&#160;million charge in </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Other operating (income) expense, net</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> in the third quarter of 2024 for a charitable contribution to the Edwards Lifesciences Foundation.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Acquisition Contract Termination Costs</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company recorded expenses of $1.7&#160;million and $9.1&#160;million in the fourth quarter of 2025 and 2024, respectively, related to the termination of certain contracts associated with the Company's acquisitions.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Gain on Remeasurement of Previously Held Interest Upon Acquisition</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company recorded a $24.6&#160;million gain in the third quarter of 2024 and a $30.5&#160;million gain in the fourth quarter of 2024 to remeasure its previously held interest upon acquisition of the investee.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Provision for Income Taxes</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - Adjustments to forecasted items unrelated to the expenses and gains above, as well as impacts related to interim reporting, will have an effect on the income tax impact of these items in subsequent periods.</font></div><div style="height:40.5pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font
